# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Fill this in as you work. It is the human-readable record of HOW this iteration was done and is snapshotted with the candidate, so anyone — and the next iteration via ./prior_iterations/ — can see your reasoning. Be concrete.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag (KNOWLEDGE / BEHAVIORAL / CAPABILITY-GAP) | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | pandas-instead-of-pivot | sales-pivot-analysis (5 trials) | Agent writes pandas groupby/pivot_table (static data) — no real Excel pivot table XML; tests check pivot XML structure | CAPABILITY-GAP | Add complete working pivot table code example with CacheDefinition + PivotTable |
| 2 | hardcode-instead-of-formula | xlsx-recover-data (5 trials) | Agent computes values in Python and hardcodes them (e.g., `sheet['K5'] = 19285`) instead of writing Excel formulas; test checks formula strings | BEHAVIORAL | Add explicit "Recovering missing values" subsection reinforcing formula-over-hardcode rule |
| 3 | ignores-existing-template | reserves-at-risk-calc (5 trials) | Agent creates a fresh empty workbook even when a template file already exists in the task directory; test checks template is loaded/preserved | BEHAVIORAL | Add Step 0 (ls -la /root/ first; load existing file if found) to Common Workflow |
| 4 | no-recalc-embedded-excel | exceltable-in-ppt (flaky, ~3/5 trials) | Agent edits ppt/embeddings/*.xlsx but never runs recalc.py before repacking; test reads with data_only=True and sees stale cached zeros | BEHAVIORAL | Add step 3b to pptx editing workflow: MUST run xlsx/recalc.py on any edited embedded xlsx |
| 5 | wrong-shape-position | pptx-reference-formatting (flaky, ~3/5 trials) | Agent leaves dangling paper title shapes at original y (~67% of slide height) instead of repositioning near bottom (≥85%); test checks y-coordinate | KNOWLEDGE | Add EMU positioning section with formula: y = slide_height - shape_height - margin |
| 6 | financial-modeling-qa | financial-modeling-qa (5 trials) | Agent consistently computes 25 (wrong); likely off-by-one or wrong scoring-category interpretation from background.pdf; no clear fix available from skill side | KNOWLEDGE | SKIPPED — see below |
| 7 | invoice-fraud-detection | invoice-fraud-detection (mixed) | Some trials: context overflow; others: output content fails test; unclear expected format from skill side alone | BEHAVIORAL | SKIPPED — see below |

## Changes made this iteration (one row per edit — aim for MULTIPLE classes, incl. a NEW tool when a cluster needs one)
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| pandas-instead-of-pivot | CAPABILITY-GAP | xlsx/SKILL.md | Added "## Creating Excel Pivot Tables" section: CRITICAL warning + complete working code (CacheDefinition, PivotTable, PivotField, DataField, Location, CacheFields, CacheField) with headers/field-index/subtotal rules | Yes — only affects agents that need pivot tables; no impact on agents doing data analysis or formula work |
| hardcode-instead-of-formula | BEHAVIORAL (reinforce) | xlsx/SKILL.md | Added "Recovering missing values in existing spreadsheets" subsection after the existing "Use Formulas, Not Hardcoded Values" section: explicit ??? / N/A case with WRONG/CORRECT examples + 5-step recovery checklist ending with recalc.py | Yes — same "use formulas" principle already in skill; only makes it more explicit for the placeholder-replacement case |
| ignores-existing-template | BEHAVIORAL | xlsx/SKILL.md | Added "Step 0 — Always inventory existing files first" above the Common Workflow: `ls -la /root/` BEFORE creating any workbook + rule to load existing file if found | Yes — only fires before workbook creation; passing tasks that start from scratch are unaffected |
| no-recalc-embedded-excel | BEHAVIORAL | pptx/SKILL.md | Added step 3b between existing steps 3 and 4: CRITICAL note that any edited ppt/embeddings/*.xlsx MUST be run through xlsx/recalc.py before repacking, with exact find+run commands | Yes — step only triggers when agent edits an embedded xlsx; agents that don't touch embeddings are unaffected |
| wrong-shape-position | KNOWLEDGE | pptx/SKILL.md | Added "Shape positioning in EMU units" subsection under Raw XML access: EMU definition, near-bottom threshold (≥85%), center-alignment formula, Python computation snippet, reminder to read presentation.xml for actual dimensions | Yes — informational; does not change any algorithm; agents already computing correct positions will ignore it |

## Verify-the-fix (one line per change: the trace it targets → what the guard/computation/new-tool now does on those exact inputs)
- **pivot tables** → sales-pivot-analysis t0-t4 all used `df.groupby().agg()` + `df.to_excel()`; the new section's CRITICAL warning + verbatim working example gives the agent a complete template to follow verbatim, producing real `<pivotTable>` XML with correct `rowFields`/`dataFields` that tests check via OOXML inspection
- **formula recovery** → xlsx-recover-data t0-t4 all did `sheet['K5'] = <python_int>`; the new "Recovering missing values" subsection's WRONG/CORRECT contrast + 5-step checklist forces `sheet['K5'] = '=SUM(B5:J5)'` + recalc.py run, so `data_only=True` reads the correctly computed value
- **template inventory** → reserves-at-risk-calc t0-t4 all started with `wb = Workbook()` without listing `/root/`; Step 0 forces `ls -la /root/` first, making the template file visible → agent calls `load_workbook(template)` instead, preserving existing sheet structure
- **embedded Excel recalc** → exceltable-in-ppt t0/t2/t4 edited the xlsx but skipped recalc; step 3b forces `python recalc.py ppt/embeddings/Microsoft_Excel_Worksheet.xlsx` and requires `"status": "success"` before repacking → formula-derived cells have correct cached values → test reading with `data_only=True` passes (t1 already did this and passed, confirming fix)
- **shape position** → pptx-reference-formatting t2/t3/t4 left shape at y≈4.6M (67% height); the EMU guide states near-bottom means y ≥ 85% (5.8M+) and gives the Python formula → agent computes y = 6858000 - height - 457200 and updates `<a:xfrm>` accordingly → `test_titles_placed_near_bottom` and `test_titles_center_aligned` pass (t0 already computed y≈6.2M and passed)

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: Serial fallback — single-agent session; no subagents spawned. Trajectories read sequentially (50 files: 5 trials × 10 tasks).
- Prior iterations I read from ./prior_iterations/ + ./RUNMAP.md: No prior iterations exist (this is the first iteration from baseline seed). LEDGER.md confirmed no prior runs. RUNMAP.md was empty.
- Diagnostic method: Read all trajectory files for each task group; identified consistent failure pattern per cluster (all 5 trials doing the same wrong thing = BEHAVIORAL or CAPABILITY-GAP; only some trials failing = flaky = KNOWLEDGE gap or environment race).

## Good things to PRESERVE (do not let a future iteration undo these)
- "Use Formulas, Not Hardcoded Values" rule (existing in xlsx/SKILL.md lines 96-128) — already present, reinforced by the new "Recovering missing values" subsection
- recalc.py integration in the xlsx Common Workflow (step 5 at line 162-165) — critical for any task that writes formulas
- The pptx OOXML editing workflow structure (steps 1-5) — the new step 3b must stay between steps 3 and 4
- The CacheDefinition + PivotTable working example in the new pivot section — must not be replaced with a pandas alternative

## Deliberately skipped (cluster + why — already-passing / needs gold / infra noise)
- **financial-modeling-qa**: Agent reads background.pdf correctly but computes the wrong game score (25 vs correct value). The root cause is a subtle mis-application of the ModelOff 2016 scoring rules (dice-roll game categories). Without knowing the correct expected answer or seeing the exact scoring algorithm in the background PDF, adding generic "read carefully" guidance has very low probability of changing the answer. Blast radius: any change specific enough to fix this would risk breaking passing tasks.
- **invoice-fraud-detection**: Two distinct sub-failures across trials: (a) context overflow causes the agent to never produce an output file; (b) output content fails test when produced. Sub-failure (a) cannot be fixed from skill side (it's an agent context limit). Sub-failure (b) requires knowing the exact expected output format (column names, row order, threshold) which is not visible in the skill space. Skipped to avoid unsafe guesses.
